recipient_name: Donald Trump (via DT Marks DEFI LLC)
basis: Sum of lines 124.3-124.12 of Trump's 2025 OGE Form 278e, 'proceeds from token sales distributed by World Liberty Financial' ($526,810,321), self-reported.
notes: Gross, not profit. About $290M arrived as ETH, BTC, USDC and other tokens rather than dollars. It includes the share of ALT5's WLFI purchase that was distributed in 2025 (row C97-12) and overlaps with every press estimate in rows C97-16 to C97-21. The filing does not say whether this is all of DT Marks DEFI's income or only Trump's roughly 70% share (see C97-15). White House: no conflicts of interest; World Liberty declined to comment.

recipient_name: Donald Trump (via DT Marks DEFI LLC)
basis: Line 124.2 of the 2025 OGE Form 278e: net proceeds from the sale of equity in WLF Holdco LLC.
notes: The buyer is not named. Together with C97-03 this is the money CAP links to the reported Aryam (UAE) purchase of 49% of World Liberty; it overlaps with C97-04. Not to be added to C97-04.

recipient_name: Donald Trump (via DT Marks SC LLC)
basis: Line 114 of the 2025 OGE Form 278e: capital contribution from new members of Stablecoin Holdco LLC and sale of its Class C units.
notes: Reuters and the NYT count this line as World Liberty income (giving 'almost $800M'); Bloomberg and NOTUS leave it out (giving 'about $594M'). It is the same money either way. The buyer is not named. It overlaps with C97-04.

recipient_name: Trump-family entities (DT Marks DEFI and DT Marks SC)
basis: The Wall Street Journal, relayed by other outlets, reports that about $187M of the first $250M Aryam Investment 1 paid for 49% of World Liberty went to Trump-family entities.
notes: This is the same money as rows C97-02 and C97-03, viewed from the payer's side: do not add. Payment of the second $250M is not documented. CAP observes that the $262.5M in C97-02 and C97-03 equals 75% x 70% of $500M, which would fit full payment; that is an inference. WLF and the White House deny wrongdoing; Trump says he knew nothing of the deal.

basis: Line 204.1 of the 2025 OGE Form 278e: 'Net Operating Income' of the stablecoin business.
notes: USD1 reserve-yield income after expenses, as reported. CAP's gross estimate for 2025 is about $26.3M for the family. Overlaps with C97-06 for 2025 if that is extended backward.

basis: Annualized family share of USD1 reserve income: CAP estimates about $140,000 a day (July 2026), and Bloomberg projects nearly $150M of 2026 USD1 revenue for World Liberty, of which 38.25% is about $57M (our arithmetic).
notes: This is gross revenue before expenses, so it is not cash received. USD1 supply fell from about $4.7B in mid-2026 to about $3.1B on Nov. 16, 2026, so the full-year figure is likely toward the low end. The MGX-Binance $2B produced no fee for World Liberty; its value is the reserve yield, already counted here. World Liberty says it does not share USD1 revenue with Binance.

basis: Line 21.6 of the 2025 OGE Form 278e: royalties of $635,068,835 under a license agreement with 'Celebration Coins'; lines 21.3 and 21.4a add $45,932 of interest and $510,808 of ETH staking rewards.
notes: This is licensing income, not token sales by Trump. Part is held as crypto: at year-end CIC Digital held BTC worth over $50M and ETH and USDC worth $5M-$25M each (see C97-14). It overlaps with the on-chain estimates in C97-08. The coin's website says it is not sold by Trump or the Trump Organization.

recipient_name: $TRUMP issuing entities (CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight)
basis: On-chain estimates: CAP about $313M of net USDC withdrawals; FT at least $350M ($314M sales plus $36M fees) in the first three weeks; Chainalysis more than $320M in fees by May 2025; Reuters about $616M for the family through April 2026.
notes: Each estimate measures something different (sales, fees or both; all issuers or the family), and each comes from one outlet. Most of them cover Fight Fight Fight as well as Trump's CIC Digital. They overlap with C97-07 and must not be added to it.

recipient_name: $TRUMP team wallets (CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight)
basis: Low end: Forbes' September 2026 value of Trump's own $TRUMP stake. High end: about 718M team tokens (Crypto Briefing, October 2026) at $0.944 (CoinGecko, Nov. 16, 2026); the arithmetic is ours.
notes: Paper value only. The tokens are partly still unlocking, and the split between CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight is unknown. Trump's 2025 filing lists no $TRUMP token holdings at all. The token is about 99% below its January 2025 peak.

basis: Crypto Briefing reports that team wallets moved about $249M of $TRUMP to exchanges over eight months; whether the tokens were sold cannot be seen on-chain.
notes: This may be 2026 cash, but it is unconfirmed, and any 2026 income will appear only in the filing due May 2027. It may partly overlap with Reuters' $616M (C97-08) for February to April 2026.

basis: Line 3.3 (spouse) of the 2025 OGE Form 278e: net proceeds from a license with Designers Manager for the sale of NFTs and other collectibles.
notes: The filing does not name $MELANIA; linking this income to the coin is CAP's inference. The FT (May 2025) reported that the coin's launch entities had withdrawn $64.7M from fees and primary sales, with Melania Trump's share unknown.

recipient_name: Trump family (via the World Liberty 75% fee)
basis: Reuters and CAP report that ALT5 spent $717M buying WLFI from World Liberty; the WSJ, CNBC and Reuters estimate more than $500M routed to the Trump family (75% of $717M is about $538M before expenses).
notes: Fully inside World Liberty token sales: it overlaps with C97-01 and with the press totals C97-16 to C97-19. Do not add. The other $750M of the ALT5 deal was WLFI exchanged for ALT5 shares, not cash (see C97-13).

basis: World Liberty received ALT5 (now AI Financial, AIFC) shares valued at $750M in exchange for WLFI in August 2025; AI Financial's entire market value was about $22.5M on Nov. 13, 2026, which caps the holding's value.
notes: Company-level paper value; the family's indirect share runs through DT Marks DEFI's 38.25% of WLF Holdco. World Liberty's exact share count was not verified here. The stock is about 98% below its pre-deal price.

recipient_name: Donald Trump (DT Marks DEFI and CIC Digital wallets)
basis: Lower bound from the filing's value ranges for crypto held at year-end: DT Marks DEFI (ETH over $50M, BTC over $50M, AAVE $1M-$5M, LINK $0.5M-$1M, USD $0.1M-$0.25M) and CIC Digital (BTC over $50M, ETH and USDC $5M-$25M each); the arithmetic is ours.
notes: This is a lower bound only: three entries say 'Over $50,000,000' with no ceiling. These assets largely are the proceeds in C97-01 and C97-07 kept in crypto form, so do not add them to those rows. Bitcoin and ether prices have moved since year-end.

recipient_name: Other Trump family members (30% of DT Marks DEFI and DT Marks SC)
basis: The filing shows 'Trump Family Members' owning 30% of DT Marks DEFI and DT Marks SC. If rows C97-01 to C97-03 ($789.3M) are Trump's 70% share, the other 30% is about $338M; if they are the entities' totals, it is already included.
notes: No source states this amount; it is our arithmetic from the ownership percentages. The family members are not named on the form. CAP reads the $262.5M stake-sale figure as Trump's 70% share, which supports the higher end for that part only.

basis: Reuters estimates $1.447B ($987M from 30B disclosed tokens plus at least $460M from 3B privately sold tokens in October 2025 EU filings); Bloomberg estimates about $1.55B including about $660M from 5.9B 'white glove' tokens sold from September 2025 to April 2026.
notes: Includes pre-term 2024 sales (Trump reported $57.36M for 2024), the 2025 distributions in C97-01 and ALT5 in C97-12; do not add. Both outlets apply the 75% fee to estimated sale prices; World Liberty confirmed the private sales but not their prices. These figures are entitlements, not payments shown in a filing.

basis: A Wall Street Journal analysis, relayed by others, put World Liberty cash to the Trump family at at least $1.2B, with about $2.25B more in paper gains.
notes: The WSJ text was not read directly. This overlaps with C97-01 to C97-04, C97-12 and C97-16. The $2.25B paper figure was measured when WLFI traded far higher than now (compare C97-18).

basis: 22.5B WLFI held by DT Marks DEFI and family members (World Liberty disclaimer) at $0.0468 (CoinGecko) is about $1.05B undiscounted; Forbes (September 2026) carries Trump's WLFI at about $78M after discounting the lock-up.
notes: The tokens are locked: under the May 2026 vesting vote, founders who opt in face a two-year cliff, so no sales before about mid-2028. The 2025 filing lists 15.75B WLFI with a value of only 'Over $50,000,000'. WLFI is about 86% below its September 2025 peak.

basis: 68,432,664 shares (Schedule 13D/A, December 2025), divided by 15 for the July 2026 reverse split, at the Nov. 13, 2026 close of $5.07; the arithmetic is ours.
notes: Paper value only; no sale or dividend was found. The stake was worth about $548M after the September 2025 listing and more than $70M at the end of April 2026 (Reuters). Reuters found no evidence that Eric Trump contributed capital. Donald Trump Jr.'s stake is below 5% and undisclosed, so it has no row. Eric Trump has disputed Forbes valuations of his wealth.

basis: Reuters (June 9, 2026): at least $2.3B for the family from World Liberty, $TRUMP, American Bitcoin and ALT5 through April 30, 2026. CAP (July 16, 2026): $2.405B from stake sales, WLFI sales, USD1 reserves, $TRUMP and $MELANIA.
notes: Umbrella totals that contain most other rows; never add them to other rows. Reuters' figure includes about $70M of paper value (Eric Trump's American Bitcoin stake). House Oversight Democratic staff (January 2026) gave 'nearly $2.25B' of profits and up to $9.72B including paper wealth, counting all $1.45B of ALT5 as token sales. Company representatives disputed parts of Reuters' accounting.

basis: Forbes' September 2026 net-worth estimate counts crypto as $183M of $TRUMP, $78M of WLFI and $233M for the USD1 business, within a $7B total.
notes: Read via Forbes Kazakhstan's relay of the Forbes estimate. This overlaps with C97-09 and C97-18. It values assets, not income, and Forbes discounts locked tokens heavily.
